title: Technology mapping (logging/technologies/*.yaml)
description: Optional, non-normative layer mapping abstract (source, event-class) pairs to concrete vendor/product telemetry. See logging/technologies/README.md.

vendor.description: Vendor slug, e.g. microsoft, fortinet, cisco.

product.description: Product/telemetry-stream slug, e.g. windows-security, fortigate, asa.

org.description: Optional organisation slug. Present => this file carries organisational context and is not assumed portable to other deployments of the same product. Must match the ID's <ORG> segment and the filename prefix.

implements.description: One block per abstract source this technology satisfies. A single appliance implementing multiple event planes (e.g. an access-decision source and a device-management source) MUST use separate blocks -- never merge their event_mappings.

event_mappings.description: Keyed by EVT-* class id. Each key MUST be a class the referenced source actually emits (subset of that source's must_emit_event_classes) -- never validated against the union of all implemented sources.

id.description: Vendor-native selector string identifying the signal: a numeric event id ('4624'), a syslog mnemonic ('%ASA-4-106023'), a cloud event name ('ConsoleLogin'), or -- for technologies with no native event id, e.g. Kubernetes audit -- a free-form field-match expression ('verb=create resource=rolebindings'). NOT required to be unique: the same id may legitimately recur under multiple event classes (e.g. Windows 4688 satisfies several). This is documentation, not a machine-parseable query -- do not build automation that assumes it is machine-resolvable.

record.description: Required human-readable description of what the signal represents.

channel.description: Log channel/type, e.g. Security, System, traffic.

mnemonic.description: Syslog mnemonic/header, if distinct from id.
